correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md reduces the matrix M_x exactly to Π+r_x(z)(I−Π) with r_x(z)=[1+(2x−1)z+(x²−2x+1/2)z²]/(1+xz)². The diagonal entry test reduces to r_x(z)≥−m/(1−m) and the off-diagonals are positive. The calculated ∂_x r=z³(2x−1)/(1+xz)³≥0 and ∂_z r=[−1+(1−3x)z]/(1+xz)³<0 give the unique success cutoff x*(z,m), whose uniform interval measure yields the exact P branches, endpoint values, and one-third stiff frontier. Taylor expansion at z0 gives the square-root onset. Because −1<r_x(z)<1 for every x in the parameter interval and finite z, the product projector representation has multiplier bounded by q(z)^n for q(z)<1; it eventually lies strictly above the diagonal nonnegativity threshold even for nonstochastic individual factors. Independently derived symbolic derivatives and exact rational endpoint tests in independent_checks.py gave CASE1_OK. Tests only support sampled boundaries; infinite conclusion is the algebraic argument. No proof claims 3-state, stagewise, nonlinear or finite-precision positivity.
